scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, requested by SH-CS).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) were billed on an ACTUAL meter read rather than an ESTIMATED read (E-02).
Field manual-read route completion ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep, covering 9200 accounts (E-01) - a separate operational shortfall.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05), and the disputed-bill population is majority ACTUAL-read bills rather than ESTIMATED-read bills (1785 vs 1240 of 3025, E-02). This pattern supports H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: a change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills computed from ACTUAL meter reads to be miscalculated or misvalidated and is driving the dispute surge, while tariff change (E-03), slow ticket response (E-04), and field-read/AMI-delivery failures (both rejected against E-02) are ruled out as the mechanism.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-11: E-02 still shows the raw split of disputed bills by read type (1785 ACTUAL, 1240 ESTIMATED of 3025). It no longer supports a billing-rule mechanism that miscalculates ACTUAL-read bills: E-11 shows the only confirmed import-validation rule rejects high-consumption AMI reads and forces ESTIMATED substitution, i.e. it explains the ESTIMATED subset, not why ACTUAL-read bills themselves would be wrong.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: Dispute tickets doubled mainly because Customer Service cannot respond/triage fast enough, so an AI auto-answer agent would resolve the surge.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused bills to be miscalculated or misvalidated, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI) degraded, forcing more estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) became incomplete or inaccurate, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-FLAW.statement: The estimate-substitution logic used when no accepted read is available is itself miscalibrated, producing wrong bills independent of upstream read-delivery issues.

H-NON-BILLING-DISPUTE-DRIVER.statement: Bills are not more incorrect; the dispute surge stems from a non-accuracy driver unrelated to meter-to-cash data quality.

H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for the large majority (1184/1240) of AMI-channel disputed estimated bills.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG.statement: Rule BV-17 compares a raw AMI register value directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling=none; if the register's native unit/multiplier differs from m3, this would systematically overstate apparent consumption and misflag normal reads as high-consumption, rejecting them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) rather than correctly detecting anomalies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (ORG-FIELD) ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a shortfall in on-time manual meter reads during the dispute-surge window.

E-01 still shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over 2026-08..09. It no longer corroborates the billing-rule-change root cause for the ACTUAL-read dispute majority, since the confirmed import mechanism (E-11) addresses AMI high-consumption rejection, not manual-read route lateness or ACTUAL-read miscalculation.

Of disputed bills, 1785 were billed on an ACTUAL read and 1240 on an ESTIMATED read (3025 total) — a majority of disputes attach to bills that used an actual meter read, not an estimate-substitution read.

E-02 still shows the raw split of disputed bills by read type (1785 ACTUAL, 1240 ESTIMATED of 3025). It no longer supports a billing-rule mechanism that miscalculates ACTUAL-read bills: E-11 shows the only confirmed import-validation rule rejects high-consumption AMI reads and forces ESTIMATED substitution, i.e. it explains the ESTIMATED subset, not why ACTUAL-read bills themselves would be wrong.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are logged in billing-db, which rules out a tariff/rate change as a contributor to the wrong-bills driving the dispute surge.

E-03 still shows billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, ruling out a logged tariff change. It no longer helps establish, by elimination, that a billing-rule change explains the ACTUAL-read dispute majority, because the only confirmed rule mechanism (E-11) accounts for ESTIMATED-read substitution, not ACTUAL-read miscalculation.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times reports median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning current dispute-ticket response times are inside SLA, not degraded or backlogged.

E-04 still shows dispute-ticket response times (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets. It no longer functions as part of a valid elimination argument pointing to billing-rule-change as the cause of ACTUAL-read bill miscalculation, since the confirmed mechanism (E-11) only explains ESTIMATED-read substitution.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows dispute volume roughly stable at ~600/month in June-July (610, 590) then jumping to ~1180-1260/month in August-September, confirming the magnitude and timing of the surge (near-doubling) but saying nothing about its cause.

E-05 still shows dispute volume rising from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep), confirming the surge's magnitude and timing. It no longer means this surge is explained by the billing-rule-change mechanism now confirmed in E-11, since that mechanism accounts for only the 1240 ESTIMATED-read bills, not the full ~600-660/month increase that includes the ACTUAL-read majority.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that Lakeside Water may request field route priority changes but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH authority/approval constraint. It is a governance document about who may authorize push_route_update, not evidence about the billing-dispute root cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) shows 320 accounts received an estimated-read bill in the last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000/R-00). The record only links account-to-route, with no rule-change or import-status fields, so it does not test the billing-rule-change mechanism and instead is route-linkage data relevant to the field-route question.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor engineer, stakeholder) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would lift the access barrier (mdms-export tool_health DEGRADED, mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated ACCESS_PENDING) that has blocked re-testing the rejected AMI/MDMS delivery hypothesis. This is an unverified stakeholder statement about access logistics, not independent confirmation that the underlying read-event data is actually retrievable or complete.

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, AMI read-event data (E-11) shows 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff that billing import nonetheless rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (forcing estimate substitution despite a usable read), while only 56 truly had no read received. This points to a billing import validation rule that rejects high-consumption AMI reads as the mechanism forcing estimate substitution, not an AMI/MDMS delivery outage or field-read failure.

E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-12 (billing-config.validation_rule_changes) shows rule BV-17 - a high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, with unit_scaling="none" - deployed 2026-08-01, matching the dispute-surge onset, plus an unrelated label-text change BV-09 from March. This is the first direct billing-config record of the specific rule implementing the AMI-read-rejection mechanism already inferred from E-11, and the "unit_scaling: none" detail surfaces a new candidate explanation (a units mismatch) for why 1184 reads were misflagged as high consumption.

E-13 shows AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3, while firmware v3.x meters report directly in m3. Since rule BV-17 (E-12) compares the raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling="none", a v4.2 meter's raw reading would appear roughly 10x inflated under that rule, directly supporting the units-mismatch mechanism proposed for the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern (E-11).

billing-db's own import_status_estimated_disputed query reproduces E-11's exact counts (1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED) and adds firmware detail: the 1184 rejected records are all firmware v4.2 (the firmware E-13 shows reports registers in 0.1 m3 units), while the 56 no-read records are firmware "mixed" (not specifically v4.2). This corroborates the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 unit-mismatch mechanism from a second authoritative source (billing-db, not just mdms-export) and reinforces that the 56-record NO_READ subset is a distinct, firmware-mixed cause unrelated to the v4.2 unit-scaling bug.

U-RULECHANGE.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES via billing-config) show a specific rule change around August that explains the ACTUAL-read bill miscalculation pattern?
U-RULECHANGE.decision_impact: Confirms or falsifies the sole supported mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) before any bill correction is proposed; if unconfirmed, the root cause and remediation scope must be revisited.
U-RULECHANGE.resolution_path: Query billing-config change log (DA-RULES) for rule changes around August and correlate timestamps/affected accounts with disputed ACTUAL-read bills.
U-RULECHANGE.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic correlation (query_billing_config_change_log, correlate_disputed_bills_with_rule_timing) and keep propose_bill_correction as draft-only pending confirmation; no bill writes occur.
U-RULECHANGE.resolution: E-12 confirms a specific billing-config rule change (BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling) matching the surge timing and corroborating the AMI-read-rejection mechanism in E-11; it does not independently explain the 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute majority, which remains unaccounted for.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SEPARATE.question: Does the field manual-read route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01) materially contribute to the residual ESTIMATED-read dispute subset (1240 of 3025, E-02), or is it fully independent of the dispute-surge mechanism?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SEPARATE.decision_impact: If the shortfall contributes, remediation scope may need to extend to field-operations route completion; otherwise it stays a tracked but separate issue.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SEPARATE.resolution_path: Correlate the E-01 route-completion shortfall timing/accounts against the ESTIMATED-read disputed subset (E-02).
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SEPARATE.safe_placeholder: Treat the field route shortfall as a separately tracked issue outside this problem's remediation scope for now.

U-MDMS-ACCESS.question: Vendor AMI export access remains pending (recovery HOLD, mdms-export DEGRADED) - if the rule-change mechanism later proves insufficient to fully explain the surge, can AMI/MDMS read-delivery data be obtained to re-test the rejected AMI hypothesis?
U-MDMS-ACCESS.decision_impact: Determines whether the rejected H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE hypothesis could be re-tested if the rule-change mechanism is later falsified.
U-MDMS-ACCESS.resolution_path: Await vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (ORG-AMI) and re-query read_events_for_disputed_estimated once available.
U-MDMS-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the billing-rule-change investigation without AMI data; revisit only if the rule-change hypothesis is falsified.
U-MDMS-ACCESS.resolution: mdms-export query (E-11) executed successfully with AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE data, confirming AMI/MDMS read-delivery data is now obtainable, lifting the vendor-access barrier the unknown was tracking.

U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE.question: What causes the 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02), which the confirmed BV-17/firmware mechanism does not explain?
U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE.decision_impact: Without this, dispute-volume success criteria cannot be fully attributed to a known fix and the solution may wrongly claim the surge is resolved.
U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE.resolution_path: Pull CRM dispute reason/detail fields and correlate with billing-db ACTUAL-read records to identify a confirmed mechanism.
U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Report dispute-volume progress only against the confirmed BV-17/ESTIMATED-read subset; do not claim the overall surge is explained or resolved until this is answered.

U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINK.question: Does the manual-read route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95, E-01) materially contribute to the residual ESTIMATED-read dispute subset, or is it independent of the dispute-surge mechanism?
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINK.decision_impact: If linked, the route-completion shortfall becomes part of the mechanism to remediate; if independent, it should be tracked as a separate operational issue.
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINK.resolution_path: Correlate route-log completion records (E-01) with billing-db account-to-route linkage (E-09) and dispute timing.
U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINK.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion shortfall as a separate, unconfirmed issue; do not attribute dispute-volume reduction to any route remedy until linkage is confirmed.

U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY.question: Who holds authority to approve and execute a correction to billing-config rule BV-17 (e.g. accounting for firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 register unit), given no existing constraint or domain_authorization covers billing-config rule edits?
U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY.decision_impact: Determines who, if anyone, may apply a BV-17 configuration fix; without an identified authority the solution can only draft, never apply, a rule correction.
U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY.resolution_path: Check with ORG-UTIL (billing-config owner) for an existing rule-edit authorization grant; escalate to Billing Operations Lead if none is found.
U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY.safe_placeholder: Draft the BV-17 correction only as a written proposal for human review; do not apply any billing-config change.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat correlate_bv17_rejected_accounts output as provisional pending handoff validity confirmation; do not finalize correction counts solely on it.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution: billing-db's own import-status counts (1184/56) exactly match mdms-export's read-event counts (E-11), indicating the nightly AMI-to-billing handoff is consistent for this cohort, though this does not fully certify general handoff completeness/validity.

U-FIELD-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Audit H-FIELD-BILL delivery records against route-log (DA-ROUTE) and billing-db for completeness and timing match.
U-FIELD-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat assess_route_completion_link findings as provisional pending handoff validity confirmation.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, requested by SH-CS).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul: 610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05).
Of 3025 disputed bills in the available window, 1240 were ESTIMATED-read and 1785 were ACTUAL-read (E-02).

Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff that billing import nonetheless rejected as high-consumption (E-11), and only 56 had no read received at all.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05). For the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, E-02), AMI read-event data shows 1184 had a valid, timely read nonetheless rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11). This is caused by validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) comparing the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) — making normal v4.2 readings appear ~10x inflated and triggering unwarranted high-consumption rejection and forced estimate substitution. This confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG) accounts for the 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; it does not explain the larger 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02), whose cause is still unknown.

supervision.current_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05). For the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, E-02), AMI read-event data shows 1184 had a valid, timely read nonetheless rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11). This is caused by validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) comparing the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) — making normal v4.2 readings appear ~10x inflated and triggering unwarranted high-consumption rejection and forced estimate substitution. This confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG) accounts for the 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; it does not explain the larger 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02), whose cause is still unknown. proposal.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05). For the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, E-02), AMI read-event data shows 1184 had a valid, timely read nonetheless rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11). This is caused by validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) comparing the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) — making normal v4.2 readings appear ~10x inflated and triggering unwarranted high-consumption rejection and forced estimate substitution. This confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG) accounts for the 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; it does not explain the larger 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02), whose cause is still unknown.
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, requested by SH-CS).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul: 610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05).
Of 3025 disputed bills in the available window, 1240 were ESTIMATED-read and 1785 were ACTUAL-read (E-02).

Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff that billing import nonetheless rejected as high-consumption (E-11), and only 56 had no read received at all.
causal_chain: AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-13).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling=none (E-12).
For v4.2 meters, the raw 0.1 m3 register value is roughly 10x the equivalent m3 reading, so BV-17 misflags normal consumption as high-consumption.
Billing import rejects these valid, timely AMI reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, E-11) and substitutes an estimated read.
The resulting estimated bills diverge from actual usage, driving affected accounts to dispute, contributing to the ESTIMATED-read portion of the Aug-Sep surge (E-02, E-05).
The remaining 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority is not explained by this mechanism; its cause is unknown.

assumptions.statement: The BV-17 unit_scaling=none configuration (not an undetected genuine consumption anomaly) is the actual cause of the 1184 valid-but-rejected AMI reads; this rests on correlating E-12's rule record with E-13's firmware-unit record, not a direct audit of BV-17's internal comparison logic.
The remaining 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-11) are assumed to be a distinct, pre-existing minor cause unrelated to the BV-17 mechanism.
The 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills are assumed to reflect a genuine, as-yet-unidentified cause rather than a data-classification artifact in E-02's read-type field.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul: 610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05).
Of 3025 disputed bills in the available window, 1240 were ESTIMATED-read and 1785 were ACTUAL-read (E-02).

Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 had a valid AMI read received before cutoff that billing import nonetheless rejected as high-consumption (E-11), and only 56 had no read received at all.
causal_chain: AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) report register readings in units of 0.1 m3 instead of m3 (E-13).
Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with unit_scaling=none (E-12).
For v4.2 meters, the raw 0.1 m3 register value is roughly 10x the equivalent m3 reading, so BV-17 misflags normal consumption as high-consumption.
Billing import rejects these valid, timely AMI reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, E-11) and substitutes an estimated read.
The resulting estimated bills diverge from actual usage, driving affected accounts to dispute, contributing to the ESTIMATED-read portion of the Aug-Sep surge (E-02, E-05).
The remaining 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority is not explained by this mechanism; its cause is unknown.

assumptions.statement: The BV-17 unit_scaling=none configuration (not an undetected genuine consumption anomaly) is the actual cause of the 1184 valid-but-rejected AMI reads; this rests on correlating E-12's rule record with E-13's firmware-unit record, not a direct audit of BV-17's internal comparison logic.
The 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills are assumed to reflect a genuine, as-yet-unidentified cause rather than a data-classification artifact in E-02's read-type field.
The 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED disputed ESTIMATED bills are assumed to be a distinct, pre-existing minor cause unrelated to the BV-17 mechanism.

proposal.summary: The initial request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever causes wrong bills, framed as a response-speed problem. Investigation rejected that framing (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP rejected against E-04) and instead traced dispute volume doubling (E-05) to a confirmed technical cause for part of the disputes: validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none, while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report in 0.1 m3 units (E-13), causing normal readings to appear ~10x inflated and be wrongly rejected as high-consumption (E-11, cross-confirmed by E-14/E-15/E-16). This confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG) explains 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-02), but not the larger 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority, whose cause remains unidentified. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no items on hold. The DEFINE Gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs). What was released covers correlating BV17-affected accounts (DA-BILL) and assessing the route-completion link (DA-ROUTE); no automated bill writes were made (write_bill_adjustment is out of scope per the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint), and no bill-correction proposals were issued because the authority to approve rule corrections is undetermined.
key_points: Original problem framing (slow ticket response, CL-01/SH-CS) was tested and rejected: ticket response times were within SLA (E-04), ruling out H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.
Dispute surge magnitude/timing confirmed by E-05 (~600/month Jun-Jul to ~1180-1260/month Aug-Sep); disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL of 3025 (E-02).

Confirmed root cause for the ESTIMATED-read subset: rule BV-17 (E-12) with unit_scaling=none misreads firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 register units (E-13), wrongly rejecting 1184 valid reads as high-consumption (E-11), cross-validated via E-14, E-15, E-16.

Alternative causes were tested and rejected: tariff change (E-03/E-06), AMI/MDMS delivery failure (E-02, E-11), field-read failure (E-02), estimate-substitution flaw (E-02, E-11), and a non-billing driver (E-01, E-02, E-11).

The larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785 of 3025) is NOT explained by the confirmed BV-17 mechanism; its cause is an open, deferred unknown (U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE / VOB-U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE, CRITICAL).
Release scope performed: correlate_bv17_rejected_accounts (DA-BILL) and assess_route_completion_link (DA-ROUTE); propose_bill_correction and any write_bill_adjustment were excluded from scope.
No automated bill writes were made or proposed in this release, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE constraint requiring Billing Operations authority for bill writes.
The DEFINE Gate for this problem (PD-1@v2) resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS, with unresolved items formally deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved.
limitations_explained: Two verification obligations remain OPEN and are outside this release's scope: VOB-U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE (CRITICAL, why 1785 ACTUAL-read bills are disputed) and VOB-U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY (HIGH, who may approve a correction to rule BV-17).

Because VOB-U-RULE-CORRECTION-AUTHORITY is open, SC-BV17-ACCOUNTS-CORRECTED is not met: propose_bill_correction for the 1184 confirmed BV-17-affected accounts (DA-BILL) is blocked, so no correction proposals were drafted in this release.

Because VOB-U-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE is open, SC-ACTUALREAD-CAUSE-IDENTIFIED is not met: diagnosing the cause of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (DA-TICKET) is blocked, leaving the majority of disputed bills unexplained.
Execution of any actual bill correction (the write_bill_adjustment action) is explicitly out of scope for this solution and is deferred as unfinished work; only correlation/analysis was performed.

The completeness of the AMI read-event data (DA-MDMS) is UNKNOWN, and the handoffs feeding billing from AMI and field systems (H-MDMS-BILL, H-FIELD-BILL) have UNKNOWN delivery_status and semantic_validity, which limits confidence in the correlation findings.

Two open, medium-criticality unknowns (U-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINK and U-FIELD-HANDOFF-VALIDITY) mean the assessment of whether the manual-read route completion shortfall contributes to residual disputes may remain inconclusive.
